title: Pseudo-Non-Linear Data Augmentation: A Constrained Energy Minimization Viewpoint
claim: Structured data is turned into a poset, embedded as a discrete distribution, then given dually-flat coordinates by a log-linear model.
layout: Single row, left-to-right, labeled arrows between stages, dotted box around first stages
description: A horizontal pipeline reads left to right. At far left, inside a dotted box labeled 'Data', sit three small grids of numbers: a 2x3 grid, a 2x2 grid and a 1x3 grid. An arrow labeled 'Design' leads to a 'Poset Ω' drawn as a lattice of circles joined by arrows, with rows of five, five and three nodes. A second arrow labeled 'Embed φ' leads to a 3D plot of the same lattice, with a vertical bar rising from each node. Its axis is labeled p_θ(x), running from 0 to 1, and a note says 'Σ bar = 1'. A final arrow labeled 'Log-Linear Model' points off the right edge. The drawing is black and white line art, so the eye goes first to the labeled arrows and the lattice.
caption: Given structured data, we first design a poset \(\Omega \) that reflects the structure or the relationship between features. The resulting real-valued poset is then embedded into the statistical manifold \(\mathcal{S} \) as a discrete probability distribution \(p_\theta (x) \) via an embedding \(\varphi \). Finally, the log-linear model on posets provides the dually-flat coordinates \((\theta , \eta )\) for \(p_{\theta } \), which can be computed efficiently ([ref]).
abstract: We propose a simple yet novel data augmentation method for general data modalities based on energy-based modeling and principles from information geometry. Unlike most existing learning-based data augmentation methods, which rely on learning latent representations with generative models, our proposed framework enables an intuitive construction of a geometrically aware latent space that represents the structure of the data itself, supporting efficient and explicit encoding and decoding procedures. We then present and discuss how to design latent spaces that will subsequently control the augmentation with the proposed algorithm. Empirical results demonstrate that our data augmentation method achieves competitive performance in downstream tasks compared to other baselines, while offering fine-grained controllability that is lacking in the existing literature.
